channel.title: The Art Newspaper - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Art Newspaper (theartnewspaper.com)

item.title: At Frieze Los Angeles, Greg Ito’s bright baggage carries hope
item.description: The Japanese American artist’s colourful Superposition Gallery stand is both eye-catching and imbued with personal history

item.title: ‘We're the Tijuana of the tent’: non-profit Ambos's stand at Frieze Los Angeles is relocated
item.description: The non-profit, which uses art to connect communities on either side of the Mexico-US border, had to move its stand the day before Frieze's preview

item.title: The year of André Malraux: France salutes its pioneering intellectual with exhibitions and more
item.description: The author, art theorist and first culture minister of France, who died 50 years ago, is celebrated with more than 130 events, exhibitions and books this year

item.title: Danger and inspiration: Bangladeshi artists divided about country’s future after historic election
item.description: A post-revolution election has brought to power familiar figures, but change is still possible, some say

item.title: British Museum secures £5m sponsorship for Bayeux Tapestry display
item.description: The funding, from Belarus-born hedge fund billionaire Igor Tulchinsky, will help facilitate schools' access to the historic textile

item.title: UAE galleries close amid Iran missile strikes
item.description: Meanwhile Art Dubai fair, scheduled for April, plans to go ahead but its organisers are "monitoring the situation closely"

item.title: ‘Lost’ painting reattributed to Rembrandt by Rijksmuseum’s researchers
item.description: The Dutch museum has undertaken a two-year study of the 17th-century work "Vision of Zacharias in the Temple"

item.title: Blockbuster show on ancient Egyptian pharaoh Ramses II opens in London
item.description: Organised in collaboration with the Egyptian government, the exhibition comes to London in the latest stage of a world tour

item.title: Royal Ontario Museum picks new leader
item.description: Nicholas R. Bell, who previously led museums in Washington, DC, Calgary and Connecticut, will take the helm of Canada's most-visited museum

item.title: Student design competition for permanent George Floyd memorial in Minneapolis opens
item.description: The competition, open to students in Minnesota, is the first step in selecting a permanent memorial to the man whose 2020 murder set of a global reckoning with police brutality and institutional racism
